[RBND.1.3] **The dialect binding tuple.** Every DS artifact
governed by this spec carries the same three fields, each container under the
names [RBND.2.2] gives:

- `dsc_sha256`, the SHA-256 of the compiled DSC bytes that were active when
  the artifact was produced ([RBND.3.1]);
- `capabilities`, the program's resolved settings: every capability set
  `true`, in ascending `Capability` order ([LDIA.1.3]);
- `dialect_def_sha256`, the SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of those
  settings ([RBND.4]).

The dialect's name is not part of the tuple: two programs whose settings
resolve alike are bound alike, whatever dialect each named.

**A malformed `capabilities` list is refused.** The list is strictly
ascending, and each entry is a member of `proto/capabilities.proto#Capability`
other than `CAPABILITY_UNSPECIFIED`. So no capability appears twice, and the
list is never longer than the enum has members. A reader **must** refuse a list
that breaks either rule: at load, with `DS_ERR_DSC_SEMANTIC`; in a recording's
header, with `DS_ERR_PARSE`. It must not cut, sort or de-duplicate the list,
because a list repaired that way would compare as a different tuple.

**The load refusal stays although a `.dsc` is trusted input** ([RDSC.9.9]).
It is a cheap structural need of the loader: the
engine copies the list into the header of every recording it writes
([RBND.3.1]), and a recording's reader refuses a malformed one.

Together these answer the question *"is this artifact talking
about the same rules-and-behavior-system as that artifact?"*
without consulting any external registry.
